summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with a complicated urinary tract infection due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa, requiring IV cefepime. He also developed Candida parapsilosis in his urine, treated with fluconazole. His hospital course was complicated by severe constipation, managed with repeated MoviPrep and bowel regimen adjustments, and tremors likely due to infection-related myoclonus, leading to discontinuation of duloxetine and initiation of mirtazapine for depression. He experienced transient hypoxia from atelectasis, improved with incentive spirometry, and had a facial rash ruled negative for HSV and VZV. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion. He was discharged to extended care on IV antibiotics, antifungal, and optimized medications for heart failure, constipation, and mood, with plans for urology and primary care follow-up.
